# Known member leaks: read, confirmed, queued for a real fix.
#
# Format: <Class>|<Member>
# Generated by tools/scan_member_leak.py. Removing a row records that the leak was
# fixed. Adding a row requires saying WHY it is a leak and not one of the exempt
# shapes (self-deleting window, AttachDialog root, ownership handoff, local variable).
#
# EMPTY -- and round 61 had to retract two rows that were here in round 60:
#
#   CComboWnd|m_pLayout  }  Both DO hand the layout to ownership:
#   CMenuWnd|m_pLayout   }      m_pm.AttachDialog(m_pLayout);
#                          AttachDialog stores it as m_pRoot (UIManager.cpp:2257) and
#                          ~CPaintManagerUI deletes m_pRoot (UIManager.cpp:422). The
#                          window embeds its own CPaintManagerUI as a value member,
#                          so the layout dies with the window. No leak.
#
# How the mistake happened, recorded so it is not repeated: I grepped
# `m_pRoot\s*=` with GNU grep, which does not support \s, got no hits, and concluded
# "m_pRoot is never assigned". The assignment was there all along. Wrong tool, wrong
# conclusion, and it survived into a merged report before being caught.
